name: Orang laut of Rangsang island
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 6 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Kähler, Hans. 1946-49. "Ethnographische und linguistische Studien von den Orang laut auf der Insel Rangsang an der Ostküste von Sumatra." Anthropos 41-44 (1-3): 1-31 [part 2, E. Wörterverzeichnis, Anthropos 41-44 (4-6): 757-785].
catalog_locator: p. 12 (of the saved 31-page extract; page header '12 H. KÄHLER [41-44, 1946-49]'), section D 'Grammatischer Abriß der Sprache der Orang laut', subsection 'Das Lautsystem', last paragraph before 'ERSTER TEIL. Der einfache Satz'
catalog_quote: Bei der Zusammenfügung der Laute zu Wörtern werden einzelne Vokale zu Trägern des Akzentes. Dieser ruht im allgemeinen auf dem Vokal der letzten Silbe.

new_statements.quote: Bei der Zusammenfügung der Laute zu Wörtern werden einzelne Vokale zu Trägern des Akzentes. Dieser ruht im allgemeinen auf dem Vokal der letzten Silbe.
new_statements.translation: When the sounds are joined together into words, individual vowels become the bearers of the accent. This generally rests on the vowel of the last syllable.
new_statements.citation: Kähler, Hans. 1946-49. "Ethnographische und linguistische Studien von den Orang laut auf der Insel Rangsang an der Ostküste von Sumatra." Anthropos 41-44 (1-3): 1-31 [and (4-6): 757-785].
new_statements.locator: p. 12, section D 'Grammatischer Abriß der Sprache der Orang laut', subsection 'Das Lautsystem' (last paragraph before 'Erster Teil'); Anthropos vol. 41-44 issue 1-3; pdf page 12 of the saved extract
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (31 pp., text present; pdf page N = printed page N, header on pdf page 12 reads "12 H. KÄHLER [41-44, 1946-49]"). Rendered pdf page 12 to PNG and read the page scan: the last paragraph of "Das Lautsystem" (section D "Grammatischer Abriß der Sprache der Orang laut"), immediately above "ERSTER TEIL. Der einfache Satz. § 1. Substantiva als Subjekt und Prädikat", reads exactly: "Bei der Zusammenfügung der Laute zu Wörtern werden einzelne Vokale zu Trägern des Akzentes. Dieser ruht im allgemeinen auf dem Vokal der letzten Silbe." (period at the end; the scanned text file has "Zusammenfiigung / Wortern / Tragern / Silbe," but the image is clean). Quote, locator and translation are correct.…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word accent falls on the final syllable of the word (as a general rule); no conditioning by syllable weight or morphology is stated.
new_statements.exceptions: None listed; the hedge 'im allgemeinen' (generally) implies some exceptions but none are given. Elsewhere the sketch says predicate emphasis/questions are carried by 'Satzmelodie' (sentence melody), not by word accent.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level ('Zusammenfügung der Laute zu Wörtern'); based on elicited words, sentences and a few narratives from one main informant (Bedola, Sendaur village, Rangsang island, Nov. 1939) plus a Johore-dialect informant (Senen). Old, brief, impressionistic statement; Seidlitz 2007 (unseen) may refine or contradict it.
new_statements.identity_note: Kähler's 'Orang laut of Rangsang island' = Duano (duan1242), Rangsang/Riau (Indonesian) dialect: Kähler p. 2 says the people call themselves 'desin dola' (people of the sea) and are called 'orang kuala' by the Malays; his wordlist has the diagnostic Duano items desin 'person', dola' 'sea', kulu 'head', kélongo 'nose'; Anderbeck 2012: 272 explicitly counts Kähler 1946a,b as a Duano lexicon. Kähler's main informant Bedola was from Sendaur, Rangsang (Nov. 1939); a second informant (Senen) supplied the Johore (Malaysian Orang Kuala) dialect, which Kähler says differs at least in having interdental s. Glottolog 5.x does not link Kähler 1946-49 to duan1242.

sources.citation: Rozelin, Diana, Netti Zurneli & Umar Fauzan. 2024. "Dialectology landscape: Duano Sea Tribe communication at Jambi Province." Journal of Language and Literature 24(2): 344-360. doi:10.24071/joll.v24i2.7840
sources.note: Lexicostatistic/dialectometric comparison of Sabak and Tungkal Duano (Jambi); 'antepenultimate/penultimate/ultimate' there refer to positions of segmental variation, not stress. Silent on stress.

sources.citation: Baharin, Nur Fathiha Asyikin, Rohani Mohd Yusof & Noor Hasnoor Mohamad Nor. 2021. "Perubahan fonologi dalam bahasa Duano dan bahasa Melayu." Jurnal Pengajian Melayu (JOMAS) 32(2): 112-133. doi:10.22452/jomas.vol32no2.7
sources.note: Segmental comparison of Johor Duano with Standard Malay (vowel/consonant correspondences, glottalisation, monophthongisation); no mention of tekanan/stress. p. 116 reports second-hand that Yusop 2013 describes Duano phonology only as inventories of vowels, consonants and vowel clusters. downloaded via the Internet Archive (live host 404).
